data.name: Dialog.AlreadyRunning
data.value: OverlayUtils is already running: look for its icon near the clock.

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.Cancelled
data.value: Administrator permission was not given, so nothing was changed.

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.CopyFailed
data.value: Could not copy OverlayUtils. Details are in errors.log (tray menu → Open settings folder).

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.DisableBody
data.value:
OverlayUtils will go back to standard mode: it moves to your user folder, removes itself from Program Files and removes the certificate it added.
The overlay will no longer appear over fullscreen games. Windows will ask for administrator permission once.

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.DisableIncomplete
data.value: OverlayUtils is now in standard mode, but the full-mode copy in Program Files could not be removed. Try again from the tray menu (Overlay over fullscreen games).

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.EnableBody
data.value:
Full mode lets the overlay appear on top of fullscreen games.
Windows allows this only for signed programs installed in Program Files, so OverlayUtils will: • trust the certificate it is signed with on this PC (only if Windows does not trust it already), • copy itself to Program Files, • remove the old AppUtili, if present.
Trusting a certificate means Windows will accept anything signed with it: do this only if you trust whoever gave you OverlayUtils. You can undo everything later from this same menu.
Windows will ask for administrator permission once.

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.Failed
data.value: Something went wrong. Details are in errors.log (tray menu → Open settings folder).

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.LaunchFailed
data.value: Full mode is installed, but Windows refused to start it ({0}). OverlayUtils keeps running in standard mode.

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.NotSigned
data.value: This copy of OverlayUtils is not signed, so Windows does not allow full mode. Use a signed release, or build one with scripts\build.ps1.

data.name: Dialog.FullMode.Untrusted
data.value: This copy is signed with a certificate that Windows does not trust and that is not a self-signed code-signing certificate. Full mode was not enabled.

data.name: Dialog.Legacy.Body
data.value:
This removes the old AppUtili: it stops it, deletes it from Program Files, removes its start-up task and the certificate it installed. Your settings have already been copied to OverlayUtils.
Windows will ask for administrator permission once.

data.name: Dialog.Legacy.Done
data.value: The old AppUtili has been removed.

data.name: Notify.HomeKeyBusy
data.value: The Home key is already used by another program (often the keyboard's own software).

data.name: Notify.HotkeyBusy
data.value: {0} is already used by another program.

data.name: Notify.LegacyRunning
data.value: The old AppUtili is still running and may clash with OverlayUtils. Remove it from the tray menu.

data.name: Notify.NoProfile
data.value: No monitor profile is assigned to this shortcut.

data.name: Notify.StandardMode
data.value: OverlayUtils is now in standard mode.

data.name: Notify.StartupFailed
data.value: Could not change the start-with-Windows setting.

data.name: Notify.StartupOff
data.value: OverlayUtils will no longer start with Windows.

data.name: Notify.SwitcherMissing
data.value: MonitorSwitcher not found: download it or choose where it is from the tray menu (Monitor).
